title.narrative: Tax Administrations: capacity development, phase 2, Swedish Tax Authority

description.narrative: Tax Administrations in BiH have improved capacity and have started to transform into modern, trustworthy and helpful tax administrations. To achieve the objectives, there are some assumptions made about the resources from the BiH Tax Administrations: Relevant counterparts for the STA are available There is enough time allocated for the staff from the BiH Tax Administrations to attend missions/workshops and to do the work needed in between missions. Support and relevant decisions made by top and middle management when needed Close cooperation between the BiH Tax Administrations and STA staff

Insatsen är den andra fasen i ett projekt som Skatteverket genomför tillsammans med skattemyndigheter och finansministerier i Bosninen-Hercegovina (BiH). Den första fasen genomfördes 2017-2021. Projektets mål är att stärka kapaciteten inom de deltagande institutionerna för att bidra till moderna, pålitliga och hjälpsamma skattemyndigheter i BiH. I förlängningen syftar projektet till att förbereda BiH på reformer inom skattesystemet och dess institutioner för att landet ska närma EU-medlemskap. Projektet arbetar inom en rad olika områden där experter från svenska Skatteverket utbildar och utbyter erfarenheter med kollegor från motsvarande bosniska myndigheter. En viktig aspekt av projektet handlar om att skapa kontaktytor mellan myndigheterna och institutionerna i BiH för att de ska utbyta information och samarbeta mer och bättre. Det behövs för att samordna skattesystemen i landet, vilket är en förutsättning för EU-medlemskap. De områden som projetket arbetar med handlar om allt från att förbättra service och attityder gentemot brukare/skattebetalare till mer tekniska områden som förifyllda deklarationer och internationellt samarbete på skatteområdet.

The contribution is the second phase in a project that the Swedish Tax Agency (STA) is implementing together with the tax authorities and finance ministries in Bosnia-Herzegovina (BiH). The first phase was completed in 2017-2021. The overall objective of the project is to strengthen the capacity within the participating institutions to contribute to modern, trustworthy and helpful tax administrations in BiH. In the long run, the project aims to prepare BiH for reforms within the tax system and its institutions in order for the country to approach EU membership. The project works in a number of different areas where experts from STA train and exchange experiences with colleagues from corresponding BiH authorities. An important aspect of the project is creating contacts between authorities and institutions in BiH in order for them to exchange information and collaborate more and better. This is crucial to harmonize the tax systems in the country, which is a prerequisite for EU membership. The areas within the project works are ranging from improving service and attitudes towards taxpayers to more technical areas such as pre-filled declarations and international cooperation in the area of taxation.

The first project component, Change the Mindset, had as a specific objective the human resource and cultural transformation in the 4 BIH Tax Administrations. The peer to peer exchange between Swedish and BiH administration resulted in the fulfillment of set objectives and overarching goal of the project. Concretely this meant the following results were reported: Improved attitudes and communication toward taxpayers more serviceand citizenoriented culture. Strengthened internal collaboration between tax administrations and between human resource, communication, and leadership departments within the administration. Introduced gender equality tools (gender maturity model, work environment management).The administrations moved from Level 23 (Compliance/ Commitment) toward Level 4 (Integration). Level 5 is institutionalization for which gender equality is part of organizational culture, leadership practice, and performance review with data and continuous learning ensuring sustainability. Examples include: genderbalanced working groups, integration of gender considerations into communication strategies, improved workenvironment reporting routines, and leadership workshops addressing bias and staff wellbeing. Institutionalized knowledge sharing and staff wellbeing systems. During the project, all four tax administrations introduced structured routines for internal knowledgesharing and staff wellbeing. This included regular crossdepartmental meetings, joint working groups, and shared guidelines developed through the project. Several administrations also introduced internal newsletters, learning sessions, and standardized templates for documenting and sharing new practices. On staff wellbeing, administrations adopted workenvironment management routines, including regular staff surveys, improved internal communication channels, and clearer procedures for addressing workplace issues. These practices have been integrated into regular management processes rather than remaining projectdriven activities. While these systems are still developing, the shift from adhoc practices to structured, recurring routines represents a meaningful step toward institutionalization. The second Objective and Project Component, Taxpayer Service, for enhanced taxpayer satisfaction also reported good results which were confirmed through surveys. Some concrete measurable results (based on the surveys) are: New and expanded eservices Communication Strategy institutionalized with updated action plans. Stronger media presence and transparency, increasing voluntary compliance and revenue. Social media and feedback loops used for continuous improvement. In the third component, Compliance Risk Management, progress was reported to be in line with plans and expectations. Compliance Risk Management (CRM) had several concrete objectives in Phase 2. These included: Establishing or strengthening CRM units within each of the four tax administrations. Institutionalizing annual risk mapping as a basis for planning and audit selection. Developing practical capacity for risk analysis through joint pilot cases. Improving cooperation between CRM and audit functions.Enhancing crossentity information sharing and promoting a harmonized approach to riskbased compliance. Building regional networks through seminars and exchanges with neighbouring administrations. In practice the work has resulted in that annual risk mapping has now become institutionalized through the Swedish support and this is guiding planning and audit resource allocation. In addition, crossentity information sharing and pilot risk analyses were implemented and regional seminars enhanced regional cooperation and exchange. In the fourth component, which is the BEPS and Global Forum (International Cooperation in tax matters) there were several concrete objectives: Establish legal and procedural frameworks for the Exchange of Information on Request (EIOR) and Automatic Exchange of Information (AEOI). Build staff capacity in all four tax administrations and the Ministries of Finance to understand and apply OECD standards. Prepare BiH for OECD peer reviews under the Global Forum. Develop technical and operational systems needed for secure taxinformation exchange.Improve coordination between tax administrations and ministries on international tax matters. Strengthen BiHs participation in the BEPS Inclusive Framework and Global Forum processes. BiH achieved Largely Compliant rating in OECD peer review (2024), largely due to Swedish support. Technical data exchange frameworks were established and are now operational. The result is an enhanced international cooperation and staff capacity in global tax transparency. In the fifth component, Audit Training for Inspectors, there were several concrete objectives in Phase 2: Develop a national audit training program tailored to the needs of all four tax administrations. Create a Trainers Guide to standardize delivery and ensure consistent quality. Establish a sustainable trainthetrainers system so BiH experts can independently deliver future training. Improve cooperation between the four tax administrations through joint training delivery. Strengthen audit methodology and practical skills across entities. The main result has been the establishment of a Trainthetrainers system. This includes the development of Audit Training Program and Trainers Guide. The trainings were organized jointly between the tax administrations. Overall achievement of objective can be defined as sustainable national audit training capacity is established and with consistent quality standards across entities. The final component (component 6) was added in the last year of the project is the sustainability of results. Within this anchoring component, it was reported that a selfassessment framework was adopted by all TAs for future planning and so called "synergy seminars" created in order to establish crosscomponent cooperation. This has resulted in better integration between the components, for example the Compliance Risk Managerment now supports Taxpayer Service and HR reform. The overall exit was implemented smoothly by Swedish Tax Agency. Unexpected Results Area Interadministration collaboration was unexpected. Reportedly there was an unprecedented cooperation between the four TAs, such as regular high level meetings, joint guidelines, and crossentity risk planning. Please check section 1.7 for more information. Gender equality mainstreaming was more advanced than anticipated. Digitalization momentum and progress was also noted. Significant rise in digital service uptake (e.g., >70% efiling), despite limited focus on IT infrastructure. The increase in digital service uptake had several important effects: it improved taxpayer convenience and voluntary compliance, reduced administrative workload, strengthened data quality for risk management and audit, and increased transparency by reducing facetoface interactions. The shift also enhanced the credibility of the tax administrations and created internal momentum for further modernization, despite limited ITfocused support in the project. Regional influence was also reported as an unexpected result. BiH TAs gained recognition and began peersharing regionally (joint regional conferences with Albania, Moldova). COVID19 adaptation was unexpected. Early online missions turned into a successful hybrid working model, later used for regional coordination.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
